items.title: [Bench] Add hybrid KV-cache geometry reference oracle
items.body:
## Summary

- add an engine-neutral reference model for mixed KV-cache block geometry
- differential-test production token-range slicing and sliding-window downsampling with deterministic Hypothesis generators
- cross-check compressed logical-token to physical-slot calculations against `KernelGroupInfo.calculate_slots`
- fail closed in the oracle on misaligned ranges, malformed/short block tables, duplicate or sparse group IDs, and incompatible slot geometry
- include a reviewer-runnable Run-All notebook and a bounded 10,000-case E2E driver

## Why

Hybrid/recurrent models can combine multiple engine block-address spaces, different `tokens_per_block`, compressed physical slots, and per-group sliding windows. Existing fixed examples cover important known shapes, but do not exercise their cross-product or provide an independent reference implementation.

The oracle deliberately enumerates logical token positions rather than sharing LMCache's optimized slicing code. That makes it useful for catching offset, unit, and per-group indexing regressions without changing runtime behavior.

## Reviewer reproduction

Install test dependencies (this PR adds Hypothesis to `requirements/test.txt`), then either Run All:

- [`benchmarks/microbenchmark/hybrid_geometry_reference.ipynb`](https://github.com/0z5a/LMCache/blob/test/hybrid-geometry-reference-oracle/benchmarks/microbenchmark/hybrid_geometry_reference.ipynb)

or run the same bounded differential driver directly:

```bash
python -m benchmarks.microbenchmark.hybrid_geometry_reference_e2e \
  --cases 10000 \
  --seed 20260904

items.title: [SGLang][MP] Preserve cache_salt across external KV operations
items.body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Fixes #4825. Companion issue: sgl-project/sglang#37160. Companion draft PR: sgl-project/sglang#37229.

The existing SGLang multi-process connector builds LMCache IPC keys without the request's `cache_salt`. Different tenants using identical token sequences can therefore resolve to the same external `ObjectKey`, even though the multiprocess key and storage layers already support salted identities.

This change:

- adds a backwards-compatible `cache_salt: str = ""` field to SGLang store metadata and argument to `lookup_kv`;
- captures the lookup salt once in `_PendingLookup`;
- reuses that salt for RETRIEVE, rescheduling cleanup, `release_pending`, `end_session`, and failure cleanup;
- includes metadata salt in synchronous and asynchronous STORE keys;
- advertises `supports_cache_salt = True` so SGLang can avoid silently using token-only keys with older connectors; and
- documents the existing IPC salt constraints.

Empty defaults preserve existing unsalted SGLang callers and serialized key behavior.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

This PR targets the currently shipped SGLang MP connector. Draft #4828 already models salt in its new unified connector. If that connector is intended to replace the existing path rather than coexist with it, I can adjust the scope accordingly.

Validation:

24 passed

pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/v1 tests/v1/test_sglang_adapter.py

```

The initial scope is MP mode only. IP mode and `extra_key` / LoRA execution namespacing require separate designs and remain follow-ups.

items.title: feat(mp): enable per-layer KV cache load for LMCache-driven MP mode
items.body:
Add per-layer (layerwise) KV cache transfer to LMCache-driven multiprocess mode so vLLM can overlap attention compute with the H2D transfer, instead of blocking on a single per-chunk (all layers per-request) transfer before the forward pass starts.

The feature is selected at runtime for CUDA. It activates only when the cache server is started with --layerwise-batch N for N > 0 and vLLM is pointed at the layerwise connector through kv_connector_module_path like below example.

lmcache server --layerwise-batch 8 --l1-size-gb 20 --eviction-policy LRU --port 5555

vllm serve --kv-transfer-config \
'{"kv_connector":"LMCacheLayerwiseMPConnector",
"kv_connector_module_path":"lmcache.integration.vllm.lmcache_mp_connector_layerwise", "kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"lmcache.mp.host": "tcp://localhost","lmcache.mp.port":5555}}'

Separate code path:
- lmcache_mp_connector_layerwise.py and vllm_multi_process_adapter_layerwise.py subclass the existing connector and worker adapter.
- modules/lmcache_layerwise_transfer.py subclasses LMCacheDrivenTransferModule and imports the helpers it reuses. lmcache_driven_transfer.py only does a minor change to accommodate per-layer path.
- protocols/layerwise.py declares REGISTER_LAYERWISE_IPC_EVENT_POOL and RETRIEVE_LAYERWISE for clear boundary without impacting existing request types.
- transfer_context/worker_layerwise_transfer.py and layerwise_futures.py hold the worker-side context and future.
- csrc/cuda/mp_mem_kernels_layerwise.cu holds the layerwise kernel and its launch code. The device helpers it shares with the per-chunk path moved verbatim into mp_mem_kernels_device.cuh, so both translation units include them rather than duplicating them.

Extension points added to existing files:
- LMCacheDrivenTransferModule.retrieve() routes every object-group copy through a new _transfer_object_group() hook so the subclass avoids hundreds of lines of duplicated code. The base implementation just calls transfer_kv_per_object_group in lmcache_driven_transfer.py.
- LMCacheMPConnector._worker_adapter_cls and LMCacheMPWorkerAdapter._create_transfer_context let the subclasses swap in their own components.
- server._build_modules selects the layerwise module when --layerwise-batch > 0

Multi-frame responses:
- MessagingFuture gains deliver() which reports whether a request is complete, and a blocking handler may declare a response_channel parameter to answer with more than one frame. Buffering intermediate frames and deciding when the exchange ends happens inside LayerwiseDeviceMessagingFuture.
- LayerwiseDeviceMessagingFuture intercepts frames by installing itself as the raw future's delivery sink, and that has to happen before the request reaches the wire. Add tests/v1/multiprocess/test_layerwise_retrieve_submit_ordering.py.

Layout:
PageBufferShapeDesc gains kv_interleaved. When set, an LMCache object uses the L2TD layout [L, 2, T, D] (K0,V0,K1,V1,...) instead of the default 2LTD layout [2, L, T, D] (all K then all V), so a per-layer transfer reads one contiguous span per layer. The flag is fixed at registration time to keep it off the per-request path.

Event pool:
EventPool in platform/base/event_pool.py allocates EVENT_POOL_SIZE IPC events once and exports their handles during REGISTER_LAYERWISE_IPC_EVENT_POOL, so the per-layer path signals a pooled event by index instead of exporting a handle per layer.

Mode exclusivity:
The two modes (per-layer and per-chunk) are mutually exclusive per server node, and the worker's mode is fixed at process start by the connector vLLM imports, not negotiated during registration.

items.title: [BugFix] Recover local disk KV cache after restart (#1175)
items.body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Fixes #1175. `LocalDiskBackend` wrote KV chunks to disk but kept its chunk
index only in memory (`self.dict`). After a process restart the index was
empty, so `contains()` missed for chunks that were still on disk, and vLLM
recomputed the prefix and re-wrote identical KV instead of reusing it. This
defeats the purpose of disk offload across restarts and, with the builtin
prefix hash, silently fills the disk with duplicate-content files.

This PR makes disk KV reusable across a restart:

- **Self-describing chunks**: on store, write a small sidecar `<chunk>.pt.meta`
  (JSON: shape / dtype / format / size / cached_positions) next to the `.pt`.
  The `.pt` holds raw bytes only, so the metadata needed to reconstruct a
  `MemoryObj` must be persisted separately. Sidecar writes are atomic
  (temp file + `os.replace`) so a crash never leaves a half-written sidecar.
- **Lazy recovery on lookup**: when an in-memory lookup misses, check the
  deterministic on-disk `.pt` and its sidecar; if both exist, rebuild the
  `DiskCacheMetadata` and register it (with correct size / usage / policy
  accounting). Wired into both lookup entry points, `contains()` and
  `batched_async_contains()`. In-flight writes are skipped
  (`exists_in_put_tasks`), and the sidecar is removed on eviction.

This is the lazy filesystem-query direction suggested on #1175 (no central
manifest, so no manifest consistency / path-traversal surface).

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Verified with a real vLLM restart (offline `LLM`, `LMCacheConnectorV1`,
  disk-only offload). Same prompt, store in one process, load in a fresh one:

  | Model | Tokens reused after restart (before -> after) | Retrieve throughput |
  |-------|-----------------------------------------------|---------------------|
  | Qwen2.5-0.5B      | 0 -> 25,856 / 26,009 | -            |
  | Qwen2.5-Coder-3B  | 0 -> 11,008 / 11,009 | 17.1 GB/s    |
  | MegaBeam-Mistral-7B | 0 -> 53,760 / 54,011 | 24.3 GB/s  |
  | Qwen2.5-Coder-32B | 0 -> 11,008 / 11,009 | 23.6 GB/s    |

  Before the fix every reload is a full miss (0 reused). The trailing partial
  chunk is not stored (`save_unfull_chunk=False`), hence the small remainder.

- Cross-restart reuse also requires a stable prefix hash across processes. With
  the builtin hash, `PYTHONHASHSEED` must be set consistently
  (as documented in `token_database.py`); otherwise keys differ per process and
  nothing is reusable regardless of this fix.

**Relationship to #2734**: This overlaps with the earlier (now stale) #2734 by @DongDongJu, which I studied before writing this. That PR explored a metadata manifest and grew large; this one deliberately takes the lighter lazy-recovery + per-chunk sidecar route (no central manifest, so none of the manifest consistency / path-traversal concerns raised there) and keeps the diff small. Happy to consolidate if the maintainers prefer one direction.

items.title: [MP] Publish coordinator-admitted cache events as vLLM KV events for KV-cache-aware routers
items.body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

In MP mode no KV-cache-aware router can see where LMCache holds KV: the MP connectors stub `take_events()`, and the MP server's placement stream (`L1_WRITE_FINISHED`, `L1_KEYS_EVICTED`, `L2_KEYS_STORED/DELETED` + `MP_TOKENS`) only reaches the coordinator's key directory over `POST /events`. Routers such as llm-d's EPP and Dynamo's KV indexer learn placements exclusively from engine ZMQ KV events, so every LMCache tier is invisible to routing (#3532 for llm-d, #4352 for Dynamo).

This implements the emitter half of RFC #4770: `ZmqKVEventPublisher`, a `CacheEventConsumer` behind the **coordinator's** ingest gate, re-publishes every admitted `CacheEventBatch` in vLLM `KVEventBatch` msgpack wire format on a ZMQ PUB socket (`kv@<emitter_id>@<model>`, 3-frame `[topic, seq, payload]`). Routers that already consume vLLM KV events index LMCache L1/L2 next to the engines' GPU tier with no adapter change; nothing in the wire format is router-specific. LMCache emits locality hints only — it does not route (#4085).

Mounting on the coordinator gives routers one fleet-wide stream that is already seq-deduplicated and incarnation-fenced. MP servers need no new flags.

- `mp_coordinator/kv_event_publisher.py` (new): `consume` → `BlockStored` (with `token_ids`, `parent_block_hash`) / `BlockRemoved`; `fence_instance` → `AllBlocksCleared` per model; `medium` = `lmcache-l1` / `lmcache-l2-<backend>`; topic identity = reporting `instance_id` (deploy as `node:<nodeName>`) or `pool:<backend>` for shared L2; non-blocking PUB, optional vLLM-style replay ring. Tokenless STOREs are skipped, DELETEs never.
- `app.py`: registered as the last broadcaster consumer when `--kv-events-endpoint` is set; closed in the lifespan.
- `mp_coordinator/config.py`, `cli/commands/coordinator.py`: `--kv-events-endpoint`, `--kv-events-replay-port`.
- `cache_events.py` / `api.py`: `parent_hash_hex` on `CacheEventEntry`, chained within one `mp.tokens` event — the only MP-server-side change.
- Docs: `docs/design/v1/mp_coordinator/cache_events.md`, `ingest.md`, `docs/source/mp/coordinator.rst`.

Companion (optional, not a dependency): llm-d/llm-d-router#2586 expands `node:`/`pool:` identities to endpoints.

Refs #4352, #4085, #4226, #3532

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

Follow-ups tracked in the RFC: shared-L2 placements are published once per reporting node (routers refcount per `pool:` identity); replay answers from the message ring, not the directory.

Golden payloads are hex constants in `test_kv_event_publisher.py` and decode unchanged with llm-d's `VLLMAdapter.ParseMessage`.

items.title: fix(kv-events): stop KV-cache-store events from carrying an extra token (#4543)
items.body:
Fixes #4543.

`ChunkedTokenDatabase.process_tokens` yields half-open `[start, end)` bounds and every consumer treats them that way — except the KV-event path. `convert_tokens_to_list` is **inclusive** of its end index by design (`tokens[token_start : token_end + 1]`, pinned by `tests/test_utils.py`), and both store paths passed the exclusive `end` straight through.

## What was wrong

**1. Every non-final event carried `block_size + 1` tokens** (`cache_engine.py:535` and the layerwise path at `:718`)

With `chunk_size=4` and 10 tokens, on `dev` today:

```
start=0 end=4  block_size=4  len(token_ids)=5  ids=[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]   <-- spills into the next chunk
start=4 end=8  block_size=4  len(token_ids)=5  ids=[4, 5, 6, 7, 8]   <-- spills into the next chunk
start=8 end=10 block_size=2  len(token_ids)=2  ids=[8, 9]            (only correct because the slice clamps)
```

`CacheStoreEvent` mirrors vLLM's `BlockStored` and is published externally through `get_kv_events()`, so the event was self-inconsistent (`len(token_ids) != block_size`) and any subscriber recomputing block hashes from `token_ids` derived different hashes than LMCache stored under.

**2. The hashes variant indexed a per-chunk list with token offsets** (`cache_engine.py:543`)

```python
stored_event.token_ids = hashes[start : end + 1]
```

`hashes` has one entry per **chunk**; `start`/`end` are **token** offsets. Measured on `dev` with two 256-token chunks:

```
start=0   end=256  key.chunk_hash=1111  hashes[start:end+1] = [1111, 2222]   <-- both hashes
start=256 end=512  key.chunk_hash=2222  hashes[start:end+1] = []             <-- none
```

## The fix

- New `convert_token_range_to_list(tokens, start, end)` in `lmcache/utils.py` takes the half-open range the token database actually yields and delegates to the existing inclusive `convert_tokens_to_list`. Both KV-event sites now call it, so the off-by-one cannot be reintroduced at a third call site. `convert_tokens_to_list` itself is unchanged — its inclusive contract and its tests stay exactly as they are.
- The hashes variant now uses `[key.chunk_hash]`. In `process_tokens`' hashes branch the key is built by `_make_key_by_hash(hash_val, ...)`, so `key.chunk_hash` *is* this chunk's entry from `hashes` — no index arithmetic needed.

## Tests

Two CPU-only regression tests in `tests/v1/test_token_database.py`, driving the real `ChunkedTokenDatabase`:

- `test_kv_event_token_ids_cover_exactly_one_chunk` — asserts `token_ids == tokens[start:end]` and `len(token_ids) == end - start` for every chunk, parametrized over `chunk_size` 4 and 16.
- `test_kv_event_chunk_hash_matches_supplied_hashes` — asserts each event's hash is that chunk's entry.

Verified locally (Python 3.12, torch 2.5.1, CPU-only):

```
3 passed
```

and confirmed they actually guard the fix — reverting `convert_token_range_to_list` to pass `end` through makes both parametrizations of the first test fail:

```
FAILED test_kv_event_token_ids_cover_exactly_one_chunk[4]
FAILED test_kv_event_token_ids_cover_exactly_one_chunk[16]
2 failed, 1 passed
```

`tests/test_utils.py` (the `convert_tokens_to_list` pins) still passes, and `ruff==0.11.7` `check` + `format` from `.pre-commit-config.yaml` are clean on all three files.

items.title: fix(mp): reload cached KV for preempted requests
items.body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

`LMCacheMPConnector.get_num_new_matched_tokens()` currently returns `(0, False)` for every preempted request. A resumed request therefore recomputes its prompt and generated-token prefix even when those KV chunks are available in LMCache.

This PR removes that early return and lets preempted requests use the existing MP lookup/load path. The connector already rebuilds the request tracker after preemption from `request.all_token_ids`, so the lookup covers both prompt and generated tokens.

Scope: this PR only enables reload of KV chunks that are already durable in LMCache. It does not change STORE completion ordering or GPU block lifetime, and it should not be treated as making arbitrary or cooperative preemption storage-safe. STORE lifetime safety and broader worker/metadata lifecycle coverage will be addressed in a separate follow-up PR after aligning on the operation-level contract.

For preempted full-sequence hits, this PR leaves the final token for vLLM to recompute logits. #3322 proposes the same last-token handling for the general full-prompt-hit path.

Refs #2007 and #2929.

Added scheduler-side tests for:

- loading a cached prompt/output prefix after preemption;
- polling an asynchronous lookup without resetting the fresh tracker;
- recomputing the final token on a preempted full-sequence hit.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

Validated on an NVIDIA H20 against LMCache `48dd4df6` with vLLM `0.27.2rc1.dev150+g311b3513a`:

items.title: fix(mp): fail fast on mixed-rank KV cache batches instead of hanging
items.body:
## What this PR does / why we need it

`wrap_kv_caches` assumes one uniform tensor geometry per batch: the wrapper
factory is resolved per tensor via `resolve_kv_wrapper_factory(tensor.device.type)`
and none of the factories tolerates a batch that mixes ranks. Nothing enforced
that assumption, so a heterogeneous batch reached the per-tensor wrap loop and
**blocked there indefinitely with no exception raised**.

Models with non-uniform KV groups hit this. MiniMax-M3 registers 60 rank-4
attention caches alongside 57 rank-3 sparse-indexer caches in a single
`register_kv_caches` batch:

| rank | shape | name suffix | count |
|---:|---|---|---:|
| 4 | `(3559, 1, 128, 256)` | `self_attn.attn` | 60 |
| 3 | `(3559, 128, 128)` | `self_attn.attn.index_cache` | 57 |

The worker then hangs and the only visible symptom is the engine repeating
`No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds` until the
registration timeout fires, which points away from the real cause. Full
investigation in #4608.

This adds a rank-uniformity check that raises `ValueError` naming each rank group
and an example layer, so the offending geometry is immediately identifiable.

**This does not add support for heterogeneous batches.** It converts an
undiagnosable hang into an actionable error. The same heterogeneity appears to
surface as a reshape error in #4263 and #4358, and as silent output corruption in
#4247, so a fail-fast guard here may help triage those too.

Non-tensor entries are excluded from the comparison: Mamba-style entries are
lists of state tensors and are deliberately left to the factories. A test pins
that behaviour so the guard cannot regress list-valued models.

## Special notes for your reviewers

I am unsure this is the shape you want, hence **draft**. Two open questions:

1. Should heterogeneous batches instead be normalized for non-Mamba models?
   `apply_kv_cache_group_edits` is gated on `kv_cache_config.has_mamba_layers`,
   so for a sparse-attention model like MiniMax-M3 the edits never run
   (`KV cache group edits applied` never logs) and the mixed batch passes
   straight through. A guard makes that failure legible but does not make the
   model work.
2. #4592 is restructuring this area with declarative KV layout descriptors. If
   that lands first, this guard may belong somewhere else, or be unnecessary.

Happy to rework, relocate, or close this if either answer makes it moot. I can
also test candidate fixes on 8x MI325X (gfx942) with MiniMax-M3.

## Testing

New `tests/v1/platform/test_kv_wrap_uniformity.py`, 3 tests, following the
existing `tests/v1/platform/test_cpu_shm.py` pattern (CPU tensors, no GPU
required):

- a uniform-rank batch still wraps and rolls back cleanly
- a rank-4 + rank-3 batch raises instead of hanging, and the error names both rank groups
- non-tensor (list) entries are not rank-compared

`4 passed` locally against an LMCache 0.5.3 install.

items.title: fix: unpin KV caches for aborted requests in sync mode
items.body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

In sync mode, `lookup(pin=True)` pins KV caches in the Worker's `LocalCPUBackend`. Normally unpin happens in `wait_for_save()`, but **aborted requests may skip `wait_for_save()` entirely**, leaving the pin count unbalanced and leaking pinned memory.

The Scheduler-side `request_finished()` calls `storage_manager.cancel_request()`, but `LocalCPUBackend` does not override `cancel_request()` (it is a no-op in the base class), so the Scheduler cannot release Worker-side pins across processes.

Fix: call `lookup_unpin()` for all `finished_req_ids` in `get_finished()` (Worker-side API) when `async_loading` is disabled.

**Why guard with `not self.async_loading`?**

In async mode, abort cleanup is already handled via `lookup_client.cancel_lookup()` on the Scheduler side, which triggers Worker-side `cleanup_memory_objs()`. Adding `lookup_unpin` here for async mode would risk double-cleanup.

**Is this safe for normally-completed requests?**

Yes. `lookup_unpin()` uses `dict.pop()` to remove the `lookup_id` from `lookup_pins`. If `wait_for_save()` already unpinned, the second call is a safe no-op (key not in dict).

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Related: PR #2786 (pin count balancing for `kv_consumer`), PR #3340 (graceful skip on Scheduler-role abort). These fix Scheduler-side abort cleanup, but do not address the Worker-side pin leak in sync mode.
- Related: PR #2045 (async abort handling) covers the async mode path.

items.title: fix(vllm): handle the vLLM 0.26.0 fused KV cache layout in group edits

labels.name: full
labels.description: Run comprehensive tests on this PR

items.body:
Fixes #4247

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

`_SubpagedAttentionViewEdit` gates on `ndim == 5`. vLLM 0.26.0 registers the non-MLA KV cache as rank 4, so the edit silently stops firing and the attention group is left paged at the backend's kernel block size instead of the scheduler's. On a hybrid-Mamba model this corrupts store/retrieve with no exception and no log line. Confirmed fixed end-to-end on affected hardware — see Validation.

## Problem

vLLM 0.26.0 changed the registered non-MLA KV cache from a rank-5 K/V-split layout to a rank-4 K/V-fused layout. All paths under `vllm/v1/attention/backends/`:

| backend | 0.25.1 — `(num_blocks, 2, block_size, num_kv_heads, head_size)` | 0.26.0 — `(num_blocks, num_kv_heads, block_size, 2 * head_size)` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flash_attn` | `flash_attn.py:132` | `flash_attn.py:141` |
| `flashinfer` | `flashinfer.py:392` | `flashinfer.py:408` |
| `triton_attn` | `triton_attn.py:345` | `triton_attn.py:351` |
| `flex_attention` | `flex_attention.py:133` | `flex_attention.py:138` |

ROCm AITER FA moved the same way (`rocm_aiter_fa.py:767` → `775`). The change is **not** universal: `hpc_attn.py:293` is byte-identical in both tags and still rank 5, so both ranks stay reachable and both have to be handled rather than swapped. The block dim is index 2 in both layouts, so only the rank distinguishes them.

## Effect

On 0.26.0 the `ndim == 5` gate is unsatisfiable, so the edit never fires and the attention group keeps the backend's kernel block size.

This only bites where that differs from the scheduler block size — backends advertising fixed integer sizes, where `select_common_block_size` descends to the largest advertised divisor (FlashInfer `[16, 32, 64]`, ROCm AITER FA `[16, 32]`). Backends advertising `MultipleOf(16)`, such as `flash_attn`, resolve to the logical size directly, so `shape[2] == spec.block_size` and the edit correctly never needed to fire there.

## Why it is silent rather than loud

Two guards should have caught a kernel-paged group; neither can.

At `lmcache/v1/kv_layer_groups.py:403`, `tokens_per_block` falls back to `bs` — the physical slot count read off the registered tensor — whenever the engine group info is absent or non-positive, explicitly so the group is "treated as non-compressed". The group is then misread not as compressed but as *uncompressed at the wrong block size*, so the `slots_per_block != tokens_per_block` diagnostic at `:691` never fires and nothing downstream has anything left to disagree about. (Trace credit: @MikeWang0316tw — my original read assumed the compressed variant.) And where the info is present, every check in `_validate_block_chunk_size_config` is a pure modulo test: `select_common_block_size` only returns divisors (`vllm/v1/worker/utils.py:344`), so the ratio is integral by construction, and a guard rejecting only non-integer ratios can never reject a wrong-but-integer one.

The only observable signal was the applied-edits counter missing a key — `{'mamba-page-view': N}` with `subpaged-attention-view` absent rather than zero, since it increments only on a match.

## Fix

- `matches()` — accept rank 4 or rank 5, comparing `shape[2]` against `spec.block_size` in both.
- `apply()` — handle both ranks; validate the `shape[1] == 2` invariant only where it applies (rank 5).
- `_in_memory_order()` — new helper. vLLM registers the rank-4 tensor as a `permute` view of the backend's physical layout (`get_kv_cache_stride_order`), which under NHD is the transpose `(0, 2, 1, 3)`. It is not contiguous in logical dim order, and pages only tile by byte range in memory order, so the rank-4 branch re-views in descending-stride order.

**Why patch `matches()` rather than move the edit after normalization.** The comment at `lmcache/integration/vllm/lmcache_mp_connector.py:773` states the edit must precede both group-info creation and transfer registration so they see the same edited views. `apply_kv_cache_group_edits` rebinds `kv_caches` at `:776`, and both `create_engine_group_infos_from_vllm` (`:779`) and `worker_adapter.register_kv_caches` (`:784`) read the rebound local. Moving it later would build group infos from the un-repaged tensor — precisely the bug being fixed.

## Known limitations

1. **Rank 4 under HND still resolves `block_size` to 1.** The edit machinery emits an NHD-shaped synthetic view by construction (`num_heads` is a synthetic 1), while the HND detector branch selects `NL_X_NB_TWO_NH_BS_HS`, whose `block_size()` reads a different axis. Pre-existing and orthogonal to the rank gate — it affects every edited group, Mamba included — and not reached by default, since `get_required_kvcache_layout` returns `None` and vLLM falls back to NHD. Filing separately.

2. **Rank-5 behavior is deliberately unchanged, including its `is_contiguous()` guard.** Extending the memory-order normalization to rank 5 would let a permuted tensor (vLLM ≤ 0.25.x under HND) re-view successfully and then be misread downstream as `block_size == 1` — converting a loud `ValueError` into a silent wrong block size. That is the exact failure class this PR exists to remove.

**Rollout note:** after upgrading, clear legacy L2 objects. The object key carries no layout fingerprint and the filesystem backend does not overwrite an existing object on store, so stale entries written by the unpatched code would be served as-is.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

## Validation

End-to-end confirmed by @MikeWang0316tw on affected hardware (GB10, FlashInfer, hybrid Mamba/GDN, `block_size=1600`). Stock vLLM `v0.26.0`, no local patches; two arms differing by this one file on the same LMCache build; greedy decoding verified bit-reproducible across two rounds.

| | patched | control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KV cache group edits applied` | `{'mamba-page-view': 48, 'subpaged-attention-view': 17}` | `{'mamba-page-view': 48}` |
| `Engine KV Format` | 5x `NL_X_NB_TWO_BS_NH_HS` | 4x `NL_X_NB_TWO_BS_NH_HS` + 1x `NL_X_NB_BS_NH_TWO_HS` |
| ran to `max_tokens` | 0/16 | 12/16 |
| flagged garbage | 0/16 | 2/16 |
| external prefix cache hit rate | 40–91% | 57–60% |

Both arms genuinely consumed external tokens, so this is not a no-op passing for the wrong reason.

The format row is the strongest signal and needs no generation: on 0.25.1 all five groups detect as format 2, and with this patch on 0.26.0 they do again. The fused format reaching the transfer layer is the bug's signature, not its cause — those kernels were being handed a group that should never have reached them unedited.

## Testing

`tests/v1/test_vllm_kv_cache_group_edits.py` — 19 tests, pure CPU, no GPU or vLLM install needed (vLLM and the spec-kind helpers are stubbed, and the module is re-imported under the stubs with a binding assert, so an installed vLLM cannot leak in; runs with or without vLLM present). Reverting the source fix turns 8 of them red with `assert 64 == 1600` and a log line reading `{'mamba-page-view': 4}`.

This module had no unit coverage before — testing was GPU end-to-end only, which pins faithful retrieve but cannot gate *which rules fire* for a given vLLM version. That is exactly why a rule silently not firing was undetectable in CI. The new tests pin the matching gate per registered layout and the resulting block granularity, not internal view shapes.

items.title: turboquant: fp8 passthrough for vLLM kv-cache-dtype fp8
items.body:
# Problem

vLLM `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` produces KV tensors as fp8 bit patterns packed in uint8 containers. The store kernel calls `.to(tl.float8e4nv)` which performs numeric conversion instead of bitcast, causing a CompilationError. The load kernel always dequantizes to float16 with no passthrough path, making round‑trip impossible.

Closes #4064

# Fix

- store_kernel.py: Added `KEY_ALREADY_FP8` constexpr. Uses `bitcast=True` instead of numeric `.to()`. Added `tl.static_assert` to reject e4b15 (vLLM only emits e4m3/e4nv).

- decode_kernel.py: Added `KEY_PASSTHROUGH_FP8` constexpr. Skips dequantization and writes raw uint8 bytes directly.

- turboquant.py: Auto‑detects dtype on both paths (`src.dtype == uint8` in serialize, `dst.dtype == uint8` in deserialize). Allocates `k_out` and `v_out` separately so keys stay uint8 while values remain float16. No public API change.

# Evidence

## Before (upstream, no fix):
triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError: at 45:56:
AssertionError: cannot cast uint8[constexpr[128]] to <['128'], fp8e4nv>


## After (this PR), full round‑trip verification:
serialize() wrote 200704 bytes (expected 200704)
deserialize() completed
key bytes match: True (mismatches: 0 / 131072)
PASS: all key fp8 bytes match -- round‑trip verified

items.title: feat: support KV cache events in MP mode for Dynamo KV-aware routing
items.body:
Refs #3661

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

In MP (multiprocess) mode, the standalone LMCache server holds the L1 cache
shared across local workers, but vLLM's `take_events()` returns empty there, so
chunk store/evict activity never reaches Dynamo's KV-aware router. This PR makes
the MP server publish vLLM-format KV cache events (`BlockStored` / `BlockRemoved`)
over ZMQ so a Dynamo-side consumer can ingest them for prefix-overlap routing.

Design:
- On store, the storage handler (where `token_ids`, `start/end`, and `chunk_hash`
  are all in scope) re-slices each LMCache chunk into engine-block-sized blocks,
  computes cumulative (prefix-chained) block hashes, and emits one `BlockStored`.
- On evict, an EventBus subscriber (`L1_KEYS_EVICTED`) looks the evicted chunk
  hashes up in a `chunk_hash -> block_hashes` registry and emits `BlockRemoved`
  (eviction only carries `chunk_hash`, never tokens).
- Hashing reuses LMCache's `TokenHasher`; the chain is carried in the hasher's
  native form and only the per-block value is reduced to Dynamo's signed-i64.
- Events use vLLM's wire format. The `BlockStored` / `BlockRemoved` /
  `KVEventBatch` structs are imported from the installed vLLM package
  (`vllm.distributed.kv_events`) rather than redefined, so the encoding stays
  identical to vLLM's and any consumer that reads vLLM ZMQ KV events works
  unchanged.
- The feature is gated by `--enable-dynamo-kv-events` (off by default) and is a
  complete no-op when disabled. Publishing failures are caught and logged so
  they do not affect the real store/evict path.

LMCache's chunk size does not need to equal the vLLM block size — chunks are
re-sliced into `kv_block_size` blocks at publish time; the only constraint is
that `chunk_size` be a multiple of `kv_block_size`.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

This is a first version; a few points are intentionally left open and made
configurable, pending discussion with the maintainers and the Dynamo side:

- **DP attribution**: the MP L1 is a shared cache across local workers, so a
  block does not map to a single vLLM instance the way Dynamo's
  `(worker_id, dp_rank)` routing expects. This PR scopes to single-DP
  (`dynamo_dp_rank=0`) and keeps attribution configurable; multi-DP attribution
  is out of scope here.
- **`medium`**: defaults to `"GPU"` so blocks are indexed for basic overlap
  routing. The MP L1 is host memory, so reporting `"Host"` for tier-aware
  routing is a possible follow-up once the Dynamo-side behavior is confirmed.
- **Gap recovery**: this PR uses plain ZMQ `PUB` with no replay socket. Under
  slow-joiner / reconnect, events can be dropped (the consumer should connect
  before stores begin). A replay endpoint matching vLLM's `ZmqEventPublisher`
  is a possible follow-up; the consumer side already supports it.

Validation (all passing locally):
- Unit / component tests for block building, the registry, the emitter, the
  publisher, and the wiring.
- a real MP server emits correctly-shaped `BlockStored` /
  `BlockRemoved` over ZMQ, decoded with vLLM's own structs.
- a real standalone Dynamo KV indexer (`python -m dynamo.indexer`)
  ingests the events — radix tree (`/dump`) and overlap scores (`/query`)
  confirmed, with blocks dropping out on eviction. This test self-skips when the
  indexer binary is not present.

## Summary                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                              
   Adds the **engine-driven transfer** path for **multi-group (hybrid) KV-cache                                               
   models** (e.g. Qwen3-27B with GDN + Attention) to the LMCache MP server.                                                   
   Upstream MP only supports a single KV group; this fills the gap.                                                           
                                                                                                                              
   This is **PR1 of 4 stacked split PRs** that supersede #3813. Three follow-up                                               
   PRs layer on PCIe/perf/wire-format optimizations on top of this base:                                                      
                                                                                                                              
   - **PR2** — PinnedBufferPool, ThreadPool serialize pipeline, async commit                                                  
   - **PR3** — torch.save wire format (~2x faster than pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)                                               
   - **PR4** — Delta-store, async-IO callbacks, LRU prefetch predictor, server re-pickle fix                                  
                                                                                                                              
   Merge order: PR1 → PR2 → PR3 → PR4.                                                                                        
                                                                                                                              
   ## What's in this PR                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                              
   - `EngineDrivenContextMetadata` extended with per-group `group_layout_descs` /                                             
     `group_block_sizes` / `group_use_mla` / `group_blocks_in_chunk` and an                                                   
     `is_multi_group` flag.                                                                                                   
   - `EngineDrivenContext.commit_store_group_raw[_async]` — new API to send                                                   
     one group's bytes via `COMMIT_STORE_GROUP`, avoiding the msgspec 4 GiB bin                                               
     limit on the combined `COMMIT_STORE` path.                                                                               
   - `EngineDrivenTransferContext` — multi-group-aware D2D pipeline:                                                          
     `submit_store` gathers/scatters per-group, serializes per-group, pipelines                                               
     the MQ submissions, joins on completion.                                                                                 
   - `gather_paged_kv_multi_group_to_cpu` /                                                                                   
     `scatter_cpu_multi_group_to_paged_kv` — per-group gather/scatter utilities                                               
     (`slice_kv_caches_for_group` to carve out the per-group layer slice).                                                    
   - **Multi-group lookup** — `lookup` now prefetches all groups (not just                                                    
     group 0), so the worker sees a complete hit mask.                                                                        
   - **fp8 dtype roundtrip** — `fp8_e4m3fn` / `fp8_e5m2` go through a                                                         
     uint8 view + dtype tag so torch's legacy unpickler preserves the dtype.                                                  
   - **Tag-tuple wire format** — `("tensor", Tensor)` for native dtypes,                                                      
     `("fp8", ndarray, name)` for fp8; auto-detected on deserialize.                                                          
   - **Group-count validation** in `_commit_store_multi_group` —                                                              
     `ValueError` instead of `IndexError` when the request references an                                                      
     out-of-range group.                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                              
   ## Tests                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                              
   15 of 16 multi-group tests pass on a CPU-only runner; the single GPU-only                                                  
   test fails because the test environment has no CUDA, not because of the                                                    
   implementation.                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                              
   ## Backward compatibility                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                              
   - Wire format is **fully backward-compatible** with single-group                                                           
     `COMMIT_STORE` callers.                                                                                                  
   - Pickle payloads from `dev<=30` decode cleanly.                                                                           
   - Storage backend format is unchanged.

First, I'm not a senior developer and created this with the help of claude and qwen3.6.
                                                                                                                              
   This PR adds **engine-driven multi-group KV cache transfer** support for hybrid models (e.g. Qwen3.6-27B with GDN/Mamba +  
 Attention groups) to the LMCache v1 multiprocess (MP) server.                                                                
                                                                                                                              
   Previously, engine-driven transfer was blocked for hybrid models with more than one KV cache group due to a hard check     
 that rejected `len(block_ids) != 1`. This PR removes that limitation and implements the full multi-group transfer path:      
 per-group layout metadata exchange, multi-group gather/scatter between GPU paged KV and CPU tensors, and correct prefetch    
 awaiting across all object groups on the server side.                                                                        
                                                                                                                              
   ## Problem                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                              
   1. **Hybrid models blocked:** Engine-driven transfer raised `RuntimeError` for models with multiple KV cache groups (e.g., 
 GDN + Attention layers).                                                                                                     
   2. **Multi-group prefetch race:** `_PrefetchJob` only awaited the group-0 `PrefetchHandle`. Handles for groups 1–N were    
 submitted but never awaited before `finish_read_prefetched` was called, causing keys to not be found in L1 during retrieval. 
   3. **No per-group layout metadata:** The registration protocol had no way to communicate per-group layout differences      
 (block_size, num_layers, hidden_dim, dtype, MLA flag) between worker and server.                                             
                                                                                                                              
   ## Solution                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                              
   ### 1. Per-Group Layout Metadata (`custom_types.py`)                                                                       
                                                                                                                              
   - Added `GroupLayoutInfo` msgspec struct carrying per-group metadata: `block_size`, `num_layers`, `hidden_dim_size`,       
 `dtype_str`, `use_mla`, `tokens_per_block`.                                                                                  
   - Extended `RegisterEngineDrivenContextPayload` with optional `group_layouts: list[GroupLayoutInfo]` (empty list =         
 single-group, backward compatible).                                                                                          
   - Extended `EngineDrivenContextMetadata` with per-group fields and `is_multi_group` property.                              
                                                                                                                              
   ### 2. Multi-Group Gather/Scatter (`transfer_context/base.py`)                                                             
                                                                                                                              
   - `slice_kv_caches_for_group()`: Extract layer subset for one group from the full KV cache.                                
   - `gather_paged_kv_multi_group_to_cpu()`: Gather all groups to a single CPU tensor (pickle-serialized blob).               
   - `scatter_cpu_multi_group_to_paged_kv()`: Scatter CPU tensor back to GPU paged KV for all groups.                         
   - Helper functions: `_serialize_multi_group_chunks()`, `_deserialize_multi_group_chunks()`.  

   ### 3. Worker-Side Multi-Group (`transfer_context/worker_transfer.py`)                                                     
                                                                                                                              
   - `EngineDrivenTransferContext.register()`: Sends per-group layout metadata to the server.                                 
   - `EngineDrivenTransferContext.submit_store()`: Gathers all groups, serializes, and submits as a single store task.        
   - `EngineDrivenTransferContext.submit_retrieve()`: Deserializes the returned blob and scatters to all groups.              
   - Added `commit_store_raw` and `prepare_retrieve_raw` to `EngineDrivenContext` ABC for raw blob I/O.                       
                                                                                                                              
   ### 4. Server-Side Multi-Group (`modules/engine_driven_transfer.py`)                                                       
                                                                                                                              
   - `register_kv_cache_engine_driven_context()`: Creates per-group `MemoryLayoutDesc` entries from `group_layouts`.          
   - `_commit_store_multi_group()`: Stores serialized blob to all object groups.                                              
   - `_prepare_retrieve_multi_group()`: Loads from all groups and returns the serialized blob.                                
                                                                                                                              
   ### 5. Multi-Group Prefetch Awaiting (`modules/lookup.py`)                                                                 
                                                                                                                              
   - Added `multi_group_handles: list[PrefetchHandle]` to `_PrefetchJob`.                                                     
   - In `end_session()`: await primary handle + all `multi_group_handles` via `query_prefetch_status`.                        
   - Call `finish_read_prefetched` for **all groups** (group-0 through group-N).                                              
   - Touch L1 keys only for group-0 (matching original behavior).                                                             
                                                                                                                              
   ## Backward Compatibility                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                              
   - All single-group paths remain unchanged. When `group_layouts` is empty (default), the code follows the original          
 single-group path.                                                                                                           
   - No breaking changes to the MP protocol for existing single-group models.                                                 
                                                                                                                              
   ## Testing                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                              
   - Added comprehensive unit tests in `tests/v1/multiprocess/test_multi_group.py` covering:                                  
     - Per-group layout serialization/deserialization                                                                         
     - Multi-group gather/scatter roundtrip                                                                                   
     - Multi-group prefetch awaiting                                                                                          
     - Single-group backward compatibility                                                                                    
                                                                                                                              
   ## Files Changed                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                              
   | File | Description |                                                                                                     
   |------|-------------|                                                                                                     
   | `lmcache/v1/multiprocess/custom_types.py` | `GroupLayoutInfo`, extended payloads |                                       
   | `lmcache/v1/multiprocess/transfer_context/base.py` | Multi-group gather/scatter functions |                              
   | `lmcache/v1/multiprocess/transfer_context/worker_transfer.py` | Worker-side multi-group transfer |                       
   | `lmcache/v1/multiprocess/modules/engine_driven_transfer.py` | Server-side multi-group transfer |                         
   | `lmcache/v1/multiprocess/modules/lookup.py` | Multi-group prefetch awaiting fix |                                        
   | `tests/v1/multiprocess/test_multi_group.py` | Unit tests |

items.title: feat: add PerfStepTimer debug instrumentation to KV cache store/retrieve pipeline
items.body:
Introduce a lightweight StoreTimer utility that records per-step latencies across the multiprocess KV transfer paths (adapter, lmcache-driven, engine-driven). All timing logic is gated behind DEBUG log level with zero overhead in production (no lock, no perf_counter call, no dict access when disabled).

Instrumented checkpoints:
- Adapter: vllm_enter → vllm_return
- LMCache-driven: ipc_server_enter → kv_sync → ipc_server_return → ipc_copy_done
- Engine-driven: enter → kv_sync → worker_copy → worker_ctx_return

The ipc_copy_done mark uses a conditional stream host callback (launch_host_func) only when DEBUG is enabled, ensuring no extra callback is registered in production.

- Tested end-to-end with vLLM and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct against a free-tier Tigris bucket using the example's serve command

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Adds a draft design doc at `docs/design/v1/distributed/l2_adapters/secondary_memory.md` proposing a single KV cache pool shared across multiple LMCache servers on different hosts, served zero-copy out of byte-addressable secondary memory (CXL Type-3 expanders, `/dev/dax`, PMem).

**Headline goal.** A KV cache hit on any model replica in a serving fleet becomes a hit for every replica, with reads served as `mmap` loads instead of network transfers.

**Core abstraction.** A `Region` behind a pluggable `RegionLocator`.
- Stage 1 ships single-host multi-region with `LocalMmapLocator` — a refactor that keeps current single-region DAX/Maru deployments working as the N=1 case.
- Stage 2 (the headline) adds `PooledMemoryLocator` for CXL 3.0 fabric pools. No changes to `RegionGroup`, the resilience contract, the placement policy interface, or the hotplug API. Cross-host extension is a locator swap, not a redesign.
- Stage 3 is operational hardening (CI, dashboards, chaos tests).

**Supporting pieces.**
- A resilience contract (six rules) that extends the L2 adapter assumptions in `overall.md` so per-region faults degrade to bitmap bits, not exceptions. Includes a leak detector test that gates merges.
- Two new `StorageManager` methods — `commit_for_handoff` and `is_persisted` — that let a request router migrate a long-context request to a host with HBM headroom without recopying the context (§5.5).
- A small adapter-private hotplug HTTP surface (status, add, remove, resize, probe). No L2 contract change.
- A unified `Region` abstraction shared by the DAX and Maru backends.

**Minimum viable shape.** The architecture is decomposable. A maintainer who wants to commit to less can land just the `StorageManager` handoff APIs (~1 PR, ~200 lines, Level A) or that plus the `RegionScope` enum and `RegionLocator` stub (~3 PRs, Level B). Both are forward-compatible with the full proposal. See the "Minimum viable shape" subsection of §11.

**Diagrams.** Mermaid sources + rendered SVGs under `docs/design/v1/distributed/l2_adapters/figures/`. Regenerate with `npx -y -p @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli mmdc -i FILE.mmd -o FILE.svg`.

## Related work

This proposal builds on the in-flight secondary-memory work in LMCache rather than duplicating it. See §1b of the doc for the inline list; the same set reproduced here for reviewer convenience:

| Item | Status | What it provides | How this proposal relates |
|---|---|---|---|
| #2788 — DAX storage backend | merged | Tiered `/dev/dax` backend | Generalized via the `Region` / `RegionGroup` refactor |
| #2572 — RFC for `/dev/dax` | closed | Original design discussion | Historical context for the byte-addressable tier |
| #3264 — Runtime DAX hotplug | open | Multi-region DAX + `add`/`drain`/`remove`/`resize`/`status` HTTP routes, generic L2 hotplug protocol | This proposal extends the hotplug surface with a migration crash journal (§8) and consolidates it under a unified `RegionGroup` shared with Maru |
| #3057 — DAX primary mode | open | Arena as allocator (DRAM-bypass) | Independent; the `RegionGroup` here is compatible with primary mode |
| #3027 — Async pin/unpin fix | open | Per-key refcount-accumulation fix | Subsumed by the resilience contract (§7, rules 2–3) once it lands; coordination welcome |
| #2705 — Maru CXL connector | merged | Zero-copy cross-instance sharing on one host | This proposal generalizes its sharing model to the `Region` abstraction and extends it to cross-host pools via `PooledMemoryLocator` |
| #2923 — 2026 Q2 Roadmap | open | "CXL improvements" and "Fault Tolerance" line items | This proposal covers the L2 side of both |

1. Whether the `Region` + `RegionLocator` shape is the right level of abstraction, especially the stage-1-to-stage-2 forward-compatibility claim (cross-host as a locator swap).
2. The resilience contract — does it capture the right invariants, and is "no exception escapes; per-region faults reduce to bitmap bits" the right policy for the controllers we already have?
3. Whether the `commit_for_handoff` / `is_persisted` pair belongs on `StorageManager` (as proposed) or somewhere narrower.
4. The "Minimum viable shape" tiers in §11 — would maintainers prefer to start at Level A, Level B, or the full proposal?

items.title: [MP][DSV4] Support hybrid KV cache manager (SupportsHMA)
items.body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Enables LMCache MP to work with vLLM's hybrid KV cache manager
(`SupportsHMA`) — required for DeepSeek-V4-Flash, which exposes 5
`KVCacheGroupSpec`s with mixed scheduler block sizes (256 / 64 / 4 / 8),
two pairs of physically identical SWA layer groups in disjoint
block-ID namespaces, and an `as_strided` `page_size_padded` MLA
layout.

Rebased on top of the day-0 V4 support landed in #3171
(`block_stride_elems` kernel + `compress_ratio` /
`physical_chunk_size` plumbing); that PR works for V4 with
`--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`. This PR adds the missing pieces
for `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`.

The work is split into eight small commits for review:

1. **Per-group `logical_block_size` in `LayerGroupIdentity`** —
   `LayerGroupIdentity` extends from a 5-tuple to a 6-tuple, adding
   the engine's *scheduler-side* block size (`KVCacheSpec.block_size`).
   Layers with same physical layout but different scheduler grids
   (V4 hybrid: dense MLA = 256-token grid, SWA = 64-token grid) now
   land in distinct LMCache groups. `_derive_compression_metadata`
   keys `compress_ratio` on the per-group `logical_bs / physical_bs`
   instead of one global `inference_engine_logical_block_size`.

2. **Per-group `kv_cache_group_id` namespace in `LayerGroupIdentity`** —
   identity extends to a 7-tuple, adding the engine's per-layer
   block-ID *namespace* handle. Two physically-identical layer sets
   that allocate from disjoint vLLM `BlockPool` namespaces (V4: gid 1
   even+MTP-SWA vs gid 2 odd-SWA) now land in distinct LMCache groups
   so a STORE op carrying gid 1's block IDs cannot mis-index gid 2's
   layers.

3. **Per-gid `LoadStoreOp` wire format + per-LMCache-group dispatch** —
   `LoadStoreOp.block_ids` changes from `list[int]` to
   `list[list[int]]` indexed by engine-side gid in registration
   order. New `GPUCacheContext.stage_block_ids_per_namespace` packs
   all namespaces into the shared GPU buffer at non-overlapping
   offsets. `MPCacheEngine.store` / `retrieve` loop per LMCache group
   with each group's own `blocks_per_chunk(g)`, kernel chunk size
   (= `get_physical_chunk_size(g)`), and namespace slice
   (`staged[group.kv_cache_group_id]`). This is a **breaking RPC
   change**: old servers cannot accept the new ops or vice versa.

4. **SWA-suffix-only store/retrieve** — for SWA groups
   (`sliding_window > 0`), store and retrieve only the trailing
   `ceil(window / logical_bs)` blocks of each chunk instead of the
   full chunk. The kernel-time SWA mask in the serving engine never
   reads positions older than `sliding_window`, so the truncated
   payload is sufficient. `LayerGroupIdentity` extends to an 8-tuple
   including `sliding_window`. Originally introduced behind an
   `LMCACHE_SWA_SUFFIX_ONLY=1` env-var gate; promoted to default in
   commit 8 after end-to-end verification. On V4-Flash
   (chunk_size=1024, windows of 8/128/256), this collapses gid 3's
   per-chunk SWA payload from ~236 MiB to ~1.85 MiB.

5. **Fix tmp buffer shape for SWA-truncated groups** — discovered
   during end-to-end smoke testing: `get_tmp_chunk_gpu_buffer`
   computed shape from `lmcache_logical_chunk_size` but the per-group
   tmp slot was sized at construction to the SWA-truncated payload.
   Mismatch caused `RuntimeError: shape '[1, 22, 1024, 584]' is
   invalid for input of size 1644544` on store. Fixed via a single
   `storage_logical_tokens_per_chunk(g)` helper used everywhere.

6. **Lint fixes** — `ruff-format` reformatted a few short ternaries;
   one mypy fix in `_build_manager`'s test helper signature.

7. **Port hybrid-on (`SupportsHMA`) to LMCache-side
   `lmcache_mp_connector`** — LMCache PR #3235 added an in-tree copy
   of the vLLM-side `LMCacheMPConnector` at
   `lmcache/integration/vllm/lmcache_mp_connector.py`, intended as
   the LMCache-tracked entrypoint users pin via
   `kv_connector_module_path`. That copy was forked off the
   pre-hybrid vLLM-side connector, so it still asserted a single
   `KVCacheGroupSpec` and was incompatible with this PR's per-gid
   wire format. This commit ports the full hybrid-on path to the
   LMCache-side copy: `SupportsHMA` inheritance, per-gid request
   tracker, per-gid `LoadStoreOp.block_ids`, `_per_gid_slice` with
   the divide-or-multiply rule for the GCD-collapsed
   `cache_config.block_size`, `register_kv_caches` forwarding
   `extra_layout_hints`, `request_finished_all_groups`, and the L0
   "primary namespace" reporting on gid 0. **No corresponding vLLM
   PR is required** — users pin via:

   ```
   --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"LMCacheMPConnector",
                          "kv_connector_module_path":
                            "lmcache.integration.vllm.lmcache_mp_connector",
                          ...}'
   ```

   The static `lmcache_mp_connector_0180.py` /
   `lmcache_mp_connector_0201.py` snapshots are intentionally NOT
   touched — those older vLLM revisions cannot drive HMA at all and
   keep their flat-list semantics; they hard-fail the moment
   `len(kv_cache_groups) > 1`, which is the right behavior.

8. **Make SWA-suffix-only the default** — drop the
   `LMCACHE_SWA_SUFFIX_ONLY=1` env-var gate introduced in commit 4
   and unconditionally publish `per_layer_sliding_window` via
   `extra_layout_hints`. Verified end-to-end (token IDs identical,
   max|Δlogprob| = 5.04e-04, well below the #13 noise floor) so the
   optimization is safe to enable by default. Full-attention groups
   (`sliding_window == 0`) are byte-for-byte unaffected. No off-switch
   env var — users who need the prior behavior can pin to a previous
   LMCache release.

Hybrid-OFF behavior is preserved by single-group/single-namespace
defaults: when no per-layer hint is supplied, every layer's
`logical_block_size` defaults to its physical `bs`, every namespace
to 0, every `sliding_window` to 0, so the 8-tuple identity collapses
to the prior 5-tuple grouping.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- **No companion vLLM PR is required.** Commit 7 adds the full
  hybrid-on path to the LMCache-tree connector at
  `lmcache/integration/vllm/lmcache_mp_connector.py`. Users opt into
  the LMCache-tracked copy via `kv_connector_module_path`, so the
  in-tree vLLM `LMCacheMPConnector` does not need any patches.
  Verified end-to-end: with a vanilla upstream vLLM (no local
  changes), DeepSeek-V4-Flash + `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`
  + LMCacheMPConnector gives 2.31×–16.47× speedups (see table
  below).
- **Backward compat**: every non-V4 / single-namespace caller hits
  a length-1 `gpu_block_ids` list, lands on namespace 0, has
  `logical == physical`, has `sliding_window == 0`, and sees
  byte-for-byte identical buffer offsets and kernel args. V3.2
  behavior is preserved (verified locally).
- **Wire format break**: protocol payload type for `STORE` /
  `RETRIEVE` updated from `list[int]` to `list[list[int]]`. Old
  LMCache servers cannot accept new ops, and new servers cannot
  accept old ops. No compat shim because the MP RPC is internal —
  same versioning approach as #3171's `vllm_block_size`-payload
  addition.

**Verified end-to-end on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, tp=4, fp8, block_size=256,
`--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`, lmcache `chunk_size=1024`,
default-on SWA-suffix**:

Probe-confirmed layer grouping (logged at `register_kv_caches`):
- 8 LMCache groups with the expected 8-tuple split:
  - gid 0 splits into 3 groups (3 dense-MLA layer flavors at
    physical_bs ∈ {64, 64, 2}, logical_bs=256, namespace=0,
    sliding_window=0)
  - gid 1 (22 even+MTP-SWA layers) and gid 2 (21 odd-SWA layers)
    split despite identical specs; logical_bs=64, namespace ∈ {1, 2},
    sliding_window=128
  - gid 3 (compressor states for CSA) splits into 2 groups by hidden
    dim (hs ∈ {512, 2048}); physical_bs=4, logical_bs=4, namespace=3,
    sliding_window=8
  - gid 4 (compressor states for HCA): physical_bs=8, logical_bs=8,
    namespace=4, sliding_window=128

TTFT measurements via `deterministic_ttft.py` (single cold/warm pair
on identical token IDs to bypass `vllm bench serve`'s seed
non-determinism):

| Mode (LMCache-side connector, vanilla upstream vLLM) | Prompt    | Cold TTFT  | Warm TTFT  | Saved          | Speedup |
|------------------------------------------------------|-----------|-----------:|-----------:|---------------:|--------:|
| Hybrid OFF                                           | 9216 tok  | 1337.8 ms  |  520.5 ms  |  817 ms (61.1%) | **2.57×**  |
| Hybrid ON, default-on SWA-suffix                     | 9216 tok  | 1321.6 ms  |  573.2 ms  |  748 ms (56.6%) | **2.31×**  |
| Hybrid ON, default-on SWA-suffix                     | 30000 tok | 2862.0 ms  |  173.7 ms  | 2688 ms (93.9%) | **16.47×** |

The speedup ratio scales with prompt length — prefill is roughly
O(L²) in attention, retrieve is roughly O(L) in H2D bandwidth. The
SWA-suffix optimization compounds at long prompts where the
bandwidth savings (especially gid 3's ~128× per-chunk reduction
from 236 MiB to 1.85 MiB) exceed the per-call gather overhead.

Correctness via `partial_hit_harness.py` (cold-pass reference vs
LMCache-hit replay, comparing token IDs and per-token logprobs):
- token IDs identical (32/32), max|Δlogprob| = 5.04e-04 (well under
  the 4e-1 threshold from the documented #13 noise floor)

Zero `Cannot store keys` / `Cannot retrieve keys` /
`chunk_block_ids_gpu underflow` exceptions in any of the verification
runs.

**If applicable**:

- [ ] this PR contains user facing changes - docs added
- [x] this PR contains unit tests

**Tests**:

- `tests/v1/test_kv_layer_groups_manager.py` — extended with
  `TestPerLayerLogicalBlockSize` (5 tests), `TestPerLayerKvCacheGroupId`
  (4 tests), `TestPerLayerSlidingWindow` (4 tests). All 34 tests
  pass.
- `tests/v1/multiprocess/test_cache_server.py`,
  `tests/v1/multiprocess/test_mq.py`,
  `tests/v1/multiprocess/test_mq_handler_helpers.py`,
  `tests/v1/multiprocess/test_blend_server_v2.py` — updated to wrap
  flat block-ID lists in length-1 nested form for the new wire
  protocol.
- All 403 tests in `tests/v1/multiprocess/` +
  `test_kv_layer_groups_manager` + `test_vllm_mp_adapter` pass.

items.title: [MP] Per-user L2 quota for multi-tenant KV cache isolation
items.body:
## Summary

- Design document for per-user storage quotas in L2 adapters
- Enables multi-tenant KV cache isolation: each user gets an independent storage budget enforced via LRU eviction
- Strict user isolation — same tokens from different users produce separate cache entries
- Dynamic quota management at runtime via HTTP API (`PUT/GET/DELETE /api/quota/{user_id}`)
- Single `trigger_watermark` knob applied uniformly: for `LRU` against aggregate capacity, for `UserLRU` against each user's quota
- Zero vLLM core changes — uses existing `extra_args.kv_transfer_params` mechanism
- Wire-compatible `IPCCacheEngineKey` change (user_id appended at end)

## Key design decisions

- `user_id` as full identity field on `ObjectKey` (participates in `__eq__`/`__hash__`)
- Server-side session caching resolves user_id for worker adapter path (LOOKUP populates, STORE reads)
- `QuotaManager` enforces `sum(quotas) ≤ adapter capacity` at set-time
- Allowlist model: unregistered users' data is evicted within one eviction cycle
- Controller branches on policy type: `UserLRU` does per-user iteration, `LRU` preserves existing global aggregate check

## Test plan

- [ ] Review design doc for correctness and completeness
- [ ] Validate backward compatibility claims (LRU mode unchanged, wire compat)
- [ ] Confirm user_id propagation path covers all code paths (store, lookup, retrieve, blend server)

> **High Risk**
> High risk because it changes cache key identity (`ObjectKey`/`IPCCacheEngineKey`) and eviction behavior in core L2 storage paths, which can impact cache hit rates, storage growth, and correctness across multi-process wire protocols.

> **Overview**
> Implements **multi-tenant L2 cache isolation** by adding `user_id` as part of cache key identity (`ObjectKey`, `IPCCacheEngineKey`) and propagating it through MP server/session handling so LOOKUP establishes user context for subsequent worker STORE/RETRIEVE.

items.body:
Refs #2961

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

We're running a Multi-LoRA vLLM setup for our civic AI project ([GovOn](https://github.com/GovOn-Org/GovOn)) and wanted to try LMCache for TTFT improvements on repeated system prompts. While exploring, we noticed that the KV cache key doesn't currently distinguish between different LoRA adapters, so we tried implementing a proof-of-concept to see if it could work.

This draft PR is our attempt at adding LoRA-aware cache keying. We'd be happy if any part of this is useful as a reference for the actual implementation.

### Approach

We used a dual-layer strategy:

1. **Hash level** — Pass the LoRA adapter name as `extra_keys` to `_hash_tokens()`, so that the `chunk_hash` itself differs per adapter. The `extra_keys` parameter and `_canonicalize_hash_inputs()` logic already existed, so we activated this path.

2. **Key level** — Inject `lmcache.tag.lora` into `request_configs`, which flows into `CacheEngineKey.tags` via the existing tag mechanism.

3. **Adapter level** — Extract `lora_request.lora_name` from vLLM's `NewRequestData` in two places:
   - `RequestTracker.from_new_request()` (worker side)
   - `get_num_new_matched_tokens()` (scheduler side lookup)

### Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `vllm_v1_adapter.py` | `_inject_lora_metadata()` helper + two call sites |
| `token_database.py` | `_prefix_hash()` now accepts and forwards `extra_keys`; `process_tokens()` extracts LoRA ID from `request_configs` |
| `cache_engine.py` | `CacheStoreEvent` populates `lora_name` from `request_configs` |

We tested Multi-LoRA serving on HuggingFace Spaces with our production model:

- **Setup**: `LGAI-EXAONE/EXAONE-4.0-32B-AWQ` + [`umyunsang/govon-civil-adapter`](https://huggingface.co/umyunsang/govon-civil-adapter) LoRA on NVIDIA L4 (24GB)

- **Space**: https://huggingface.co/spaces/umyunsang/govon-multi-lora-test

|--------|-------|
| Base model inference | 7.18s |
| LoRA adapter inference | 24.23s |
| Outputs differ (LoRA effect) | ✅ Confirmed — adapter produces different outputs |

| LoRA TTFT (1st / 2nd call) | 12.71s / 12.75s |
| Cache isolation (base → LoRA) | ✅ No cross-contamination |

> Note: TTFT speedup is not observed because this test uses vLLM's built-in prefix caching only (LMCache `kv_transfer_config` was not configured in this run). The key result is that **cache isolation works correctly** — base model cache does not leak into LoRA requests.

items.title: [Bugfix][MLA] Fix multi-group KV cache support for MLA models (GLM-5, DeepSeek V3)
items.body:
## Purpose

Fix LMCache crash when used with MLA (Multi-Latent Attention) models that store KV cache as multiple groups with different dtypes.

Fixes: #2774, #2881

## Problem

MLA models like GLM-5-FP8 and DeepSeek V3 store KV cache as **two separate groups**:
- **Group 0**: K_rope — 78 layers, `uint8` (FP8), head_dim=132
- **Group 1**: Latent KV — 78 layers, `bfloat16`, head_dim=576

LMCache's `kv_layer_groups` correctly discovers these groups:
```
KV layer groups: [
  KVLayerGroupInfo(layers=78, indices=0-77,   shape=[4734, 64, 132],  dtype=uint8),
  KVLayerGroupInfo(layers=78, indices=78-155, shape=[4734, 64, 576],  dtype=bfloat16)
]
```

But three code paths crash because they assume a single KV group:

### Crash 1: `memory_management.py` — `.tensor` property reshape
```
RuntimeError: shape '[1, 78, 256, 132]' is invalid for input of size 25638912
```
`meta.shape` only describes Group 0, but `raw_data` contains both groups concatenated.

### Crash 2: `gpu_connectors.py` — `_initialize_pointers` broadcast
```
ValueError: could not broadcast input array from shape (156,) into shape (78,)
```
`kv_cache_pointers` pre-allocated for 78 layers but `kv_caches` has 156 entries.

### Crash 3: `gpu_connectors.py` — `from_gpu` tensor size mismatch
```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (25638912) must match the size of tensor b (576)
```
`multi_layer_kv_transfer` receives the full flat buffer instead of per-group shaped tensors.

## Solution

Five targeted fixes, all backward-compatible (single-group models follow unchanged paths):

1. **`memory_management.py`**: When `meta.shapes` has >1 entry, `.tensor` raises `ValueError` forcing callers to use `get_tensor(index)` for per-group access.

2. **`gpu_connectors.py` `_initialize_pointers`**: Detects when `kv_caches` length exceeds pre-allocated pointer buffer and reallocates. Does NOT mutate `self.num_layers` (preserves transformer layer count).

3. **`gpu_connectors.py` `from_gpu` / `to_gpu`**: When MLA multi-group is detected, iterates over groups, extracts per-group tensors via `get_tensor()`, builds cached per-group pointers (`_get_group_pointers`), discovers per-group format, and calls `multi_layer_kv_transfer` separately per group with correct `head_size`.

4. **`cache_engine.py`**: Non-first-rank `lookup` returns total requested tokens when `save_only_first_rank` is enabled, so `min()` aggregation in the lookup client defers to rank 0's actual result.

5. **`local_disk_backend.py`**: Preserves multi-group `shapes`/`dtypes` through disk round-trip. Allocates with all group shapes on load when multi-group is detected.

## Production Validation

Validated on **two MLA models** in production and staging environments:

### GLM-5-FP8 (2 KV groups, `v_head_dim=256`) — Production H200
- 8x NVIDIA H200, TP=8, vLLM v0.19.0
- 3-tier cache: GPU (254K tokens) → CPU (200GB) → NVMe RAID-0 (1.75TB)
- **1.15M external cache hit tokens** under real traffic
- 500-request XL stress test (50K-180K tokens): 500/500 pass, 0 gibberish
- 150K prompt reload: 3.3s (cached) vs 27.6s (recompute) — **8.4x speedup**

### Kimi K2.5 (1 KV group, `v_head_dim=128`) — Nebius H200
- 8x NVIDIA H200, TP=8, vLLM v0.19.0
- 3-tier cache: GPU → CPU (150GB) → Disk (200GB)
- **810K external cache hit tokens** in stress test
- 145-request XL stress test (74K-222K tokens): 145/145 pass, 0 gibberish, 0 errors
- All 5 anchors loaded from CPU and disk tiers after eviction (verified via adapter logs)
- Tool call regression suite: 14/14 pass (kimi_k2 parser)

### Deployment note: `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`

When deploying LMCache with `save_only_first_rank=True` (default for TP>1), you **must** set `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` as an environment variable. Without it, Python's randomized hash seed differs across the EngineCore scheduler process and TP worker processes, causing lookup hash keys to never match store hash keys — resulting in 0% external cache hit rate with no error messages.

## Test Plan

- [x] New unit tests in `tests/v1/test_mla_multi_group.py` (7 tests)
  - `.tensor` raises ValueError for multi-group (prevents misuse)
  - `.tensor` returns shaped tensor for single-group (backward compat)
  - `get_tensor(index)` returns correct per-group shape and dtype
  - Raw buffer size equals sum of all groups
  - Per-group views reference non-overlapping memory
  - Non-first-rank lookup returns total tokens (save_only_first_rank fix)
- [x] Full existing test suite: **328 passed**, 1 pre-existing failure (unrelated CLI test), 64 skipped
- [x] End-to-end: GLM-5-FP8 on 8xH200, production traffic — 1.15M external hits
- [x] End-to-end: Kimi K2.5 on 8xH200, 3-tier stress test — 810K external hits
- [x] Tool call compliance: identical results with/without LMCache

## Environment Tested

- vLLM v0.19.0 (`vllm/vllm-openai:latest-cu130`)
- LMCache v0.4.2 (vanilla image) + bind-mounted patches from this PR branch
- LMCache built from source (production GLM-5 image)
- Models: `zai-org/GLM-5-FP8` (78 layers, 2 KV groups), `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5` (61 layers, 1 KV group)
- GPU: 8x NVIDIA H200 (140GB)
- CUDA 13.0, Driver 580.126.09
- LMCache config: `local_cpu: true`, `local_disk: /mnt/lmcache`, `chunk_size: 256`

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches GPU KV transfer, memory object semantics, and storage backends (CPU/disk) with new error-handling paths; failures could surface as cache misses or performance regressions, but changes are scoped and backed by extensive regression tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes crashes and data corruption when caching MLA (multi-group) KV layouts (e.g., GLM-5/DeepSeek V3) by treating KV as *per-group tensors* end-to-end rather than a single shape.
> 
> Key changes: GPU connector now resizes pointer buffers for multi-group KV, caches per-group GPU pointer tensors, and runs `multi_layer_kv_transfer` per group in both directions; `MemoryObj.tensor` now rejects multi-group access to force `get_tensor()` usage; disk backend persists multi-group `shapes`/`dtypes` for correct allocation on load and correct size accounting, and cleans up leftover `.pt` files on startup; `cache_engine.store()` and disk async prefetch add failure cleanup to unpin/release objects to avoid deadlocks; CPU backend adds `LazyMemoryAllocator`, proportional eviction, and a retry cap to avoid worker stalls; lookup returns total tokens on non-first ranks when `save_only_first_rank` is enabled.
> 
> Adds targeted regression/property tests covering multi-group tensor access, proportional eviction/max-attempts guards, pin-leak cleanup on failures, disk accounting/startup recovery, and allocator churn behavior.
>
